title: V-stitch — two trebles and a chain
subtitle: The lightest lacy stitch: two trebles into one base separated by a single chain
excerpt: V-stitch is two trebles worked into the same base stitch or chain space with one chain between them. The pair forms a V shape. Rows of V-stitches create an open diamond mesh — the classic lacy blanket stitch.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Vol. 2 (1887) — open V-stitch mesh in lace crochet. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776 — the open treble mesh pattern.

glossaryTerms.definition: Two trebles worked into the same base stitch or chain space with one chain between them. The pair forms a V shape; rows of V-stitches create an open diamond lace mesh.

heroPrompt: A swatch of V-stitch in cream DK cotton showing the open diamond mesh pattern, three rows visible, on a soft linen background with natural side light.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: Two trebles into the same chain space with one chain between — the V-stitch shape

content.text: is two trebles with one chain between them, all worked into the same base point. Worked across a row with equal skips between, V-stitches create an open diamond mesh. On the next row, each new V-stitch works into the chain space at the centre of the previous row's V. The mesh stacks.
Chain a multiple of 3 plus 4. This example uses ch 22 for 6 V-stitches.
Row 1: ch 4 (counts as tr + ch 1). Skip 2 chains. *(tr, ch 1, tr) in next chain — one V-stitch made. Skip 2 chains. Repeat from * across. Tr in last chain. Turn.
Row 2: ch 4 (counts as tr + ch 1). *(tr, ch 1, tr) in the ch-1 space at the centre of each V-stitch from the previous row. Repeat across. Tr in top of turning chain. Turn.

items.cause: Working into the sides of the V-stitches instead of the centre chain space
items.fix: Every row's V-stitch goes into the ch-1 space at the centre of the V below. That space is the gap between the two trebles, not the top of either treble.

items.symptom: Rows don't line up — V-stitches stagger unexpectedly
items.cause: Skipping the wrong number of stitches on the foundation row
items.fix: On the foundation row, skip 2 chains between V-stitches. The V-stitch itself takes 3 chains (tr + ch 1 + tr). Count 2 + 3 = 5 chains per repeat.

content.text: Fan stitch expands the V into a full fan of seven trebles for a more decorative surface. The granny square uses the same 'work into the chain space' principle for the corner clusters. Solomon's knot creates a larger open diamond mesh using elongated loops rather than trebles.
